metadata.description: Meet Uniglo Diamonds at the Hong Kong Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show 2027, 2–6 March. Explore natural diamonds and sourcing information.

hero.title: Uniglo Diamonds at the Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show 2027
hero.lead: The Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show 2027 will take place from 2–6 March 2027 at AsiaWorld-Expo in Hong Kong.
hero.para1: Organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council, the international sourcing event brings together suppliers of loose diamonds, coloured gemstones, pearls and jewellery-making materials with buyers, manufacturers, wholesalers and other industry professionals. Uniglo Diamonds is preparing to return to the show with a carefully selected portfolio of natural diamonds.
hero.para2: Buyers will be able to examine different shapes and specifications, discuss their sourcing requirements and understand how individual diamonds, matched pairs and calibrated selections could support bridal, core and fine-jewellery collections. Uniglo Diamonds' 2027 hall and stand number will be added to this page once officially confirmed.

foundations.title: Where the Foundations of Fine Jewellery Are Sourced
foundations.para1: Every finished piece of fine jewellery begins with its materials. Before a ring, pendant, necklace or bracelet can be created, a buyer or manufacturer must select diamonds and gemstones suited to the intended design.
foundations.para2: The Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show concentrates on this early and commercially important stage of the jewellery supply chain. Its specialist areas traditionally include the Hall of Fine Diamonds, Treasures of Nature and Treasures of Ocean.
foundations.compareLabel: These areas allow buyers to compare:
compareItems: Jewellery materials and related sourcing services
foundations.para3: This focus distinguishes the event from a finished-jewellery exhibition. It is particularly relevant to manufacturers, designers, wholesalers and retailers who want greater control over the materials used in their collections.
foundations.imageAlt: HKTDC Hong Kong International Diamond Gem and Pearl Show 2027

twinShows.title: Understanding Hong Kong's Twin Jewellery Shows
twinShows.para1: The Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show and the Hong Kong International Jewellery Show are presented as the HKTDC Twin Jewellery Shows. However, they are separate exhibitions held at different venues.
twinShows.para2: The Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show takes place from 2–6 March 2027 at AsiaWorld-Expo. It primarily focuses on loose diamonds, gemstones, pearls and jewellery materials.
twinShows.para3: The Hong Kong International Jewellery Show takes place from 4–8 March 2027 at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre. It primarily showcases finished jewellery, branded collections and completed designs.
twinShows.para4: The exhibitions overlap from 4–6 March, allowing qualifying buyers to plan a sourcing programme covering both raw materials and finished jewellery.
twinShows.para5: Because the venues are located in different parts of Hong Kong, visitors should allow sufficient travel time between meetings and avoid scheduling appointments too close together.
twinShows.imageAlt: Hong Kong Twin Jewellery Shows dates and venues for 2027

meetUniglo.title: Meet a Natural-Diamond Supplier at the Hong Kong Show
meetUniglo.para1: At the Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show 2027, Uniglo Diamonds plans to present natural diamonds for different retail, manufacturing and commercial requirements.
meetUniglo.para2: The selection may include Round Brilliant, Oval, Emerald, Pear, Cushion, Princess, Radiant, Marquise, Heart, Asscher and other fancy-shaped diamonds across different carat weights, measurements, colours and clarities.
meetUniglo.para3: A grading report provides essential information, but buyers must still consider how a diamond looks and how it will perform in its intended setting. Two stones with similar grades can differ in proportions, light performance, outline and overall visual character.
meetUniglo.discussLabel: Meeting the Uniglo Diamonds team allows buyers to compare stones directly and discuss questions such as:
discussItems: Which specifications fit a particular retail price?
Which shapes are suitable for bridal jewellery?
How should buyers compare face-up spread and carat weight?
What should be checked on a grading report?
Which diamonds can be matched for earrings?
What consistency is needed for multi-stone designs?
Which qualities are suitable for commercial collections?
Can similar requirements be supported across repeat orders?
meetUniglo.outro: These conversations help buyers source diamonds according to the needs of their customers and collections rather than relying on one isolated grade.
meetUniglo.cta: Book a Hong Kong Trade Meeting
meetUniglo.imageAlt: Natural diamonds presented by Uniglo Diamonds in Hong Kong

bridalFine.title: Natural Diamonds for Bridal and Fine-Jewellery Collections
bridalFine.para1: A diamond's intended use should influence how it is selected. An engagement-ring centre stone may be considered individually, with particular attention given to its visual proportions, outline and character. Diamond earrings require careful matching, while eternity bands, tennis bracelets and multi-stone necklaces need consistency across multiple stones.
bridalFine.para2: Buyers may also have different priorities depending on their market. Some businesses focus on higher-value documented centre stones, while others require commercial sizes, matched pairs, calibrated diamonds or repeatable quality combinations for ongoing jewellery production.
bridalFine.discussLabel: Uniglo Diamonds can discuss natural diamonds for:
bridalFine.para3: Buyers can evaluate options based on shape, size, measurements, appearance, documentation, intended setting and target price. The objective is not simply to present an extensive inventory. It is to help each buyer identify diamonds that make commercial and technical sense for their business.

shapes.title: Diamond Shapes for Different Markets
shapes.para1: Diamond-shape preferences vary between countries, retailers and customer groups. Round Brilliant diamonds remain important for engagement rings, solitaires, earrings, tennis jewellery and classic diamond designs. Their familiar outline and strong brilliance make them commercially relevant across many markets.
shapes.para2: Oval, Pear and Marquise diamonds provide elongated proportions and can offer greater visual coverage. Emerald and Asscher-cut diamonds have a more architectural appearance defined by their step-cut faceting and broad flashes of light.
shapes.para3: Cushion and Radiant diamonds combine distinctive outlines with lively brilliance, while Princess-cut diamonds remain relevant for square or geometric jewellery. Heart-shaped diamonds may suit romantic, gifting or personalised pieces.
shapes.para4: Rather than treating every shape as suitable for every buyer, Uniglo Diamonds works to understand how the diamond will be set, positioned and sold. This helps identify stones that correspond more closely to the intended product and customer.
shapes.imageAlt: Natural diamond shapes presented by Uniglo Diamonds

application.title: From Diamond Selection to Commercial Application
application.para1: The relationship between a diamond and its setting affects the finished piece's balance, appearance and wearability. An elongated diamond may require different proportions from a Round Brilliant. A tennis bracelet needs consistency across every stone, while the success of a solitaire pendant depends heavily on the visual character of one diamond.
application.para2: A manufacturer working with an existing mounting may require highly specific dimensions. A retailer preparing a bridal inventory may instead need a range of centre stones covering several shapes, carat weights and price positions.
application.discussLabel: Buyers can discuss how natural diamonds may be used across:
application.outro: Focusing on the final application helps the sourcing process move beyond a list of grades and towards diamonds that are appropriate for the finished product.

matching.title: Matching and Calibration for Jewellery Production
matching.para1: Matching becomes particularly important when several diamonds will be used together. Diamond earrings, three-stone rings, eternity bands, tennis bracelets, tennis necklaces and other multi-stone designs require consistency across relevant characteristics. Measurements, outline, colour, clarity and visual appearance may all need to be coordinated.
matching.para2: For manufacturers, calibration can also affect setting efficiency and production repeatability. Diamonds that vary significantly in size or proportion may require adjustments during setting and can produce an uneven finished appearance.
matching.discussLabel: Buyers meeting Uniglo Diamonds can discuss requirements for:
matching.para3: These requirements should be explained at the beginning of the sourcing process so the proposed diamond selection reflects its final jewellery application.
matching.imageAlt: Matched and calibrated natural diamonds from Uniglo Diamonds in Hong Kong

measurements.title: Measurements, Proportions and Face-Up Appearance
measurements.para1: Carat weight is essential, but it does not provide a complete picture of how a polished diamond will appear. Two diamonds with the same carat weight may have different dimensions, proportions and face-up sizes. This is particularly relevant for fancy-shaped diamonds, where outline and length-to-width ratio can significantly affect the character of the stone.
measurements.para2: A manufacturer may require precise dimensions to fit an existing mounting. A retailer may prefer an Oval or Emerald diamond with a particular length-to-width ratio. A designer may need stones with proportions that support a specific creative direction.
measurements.considerLabel: Buyers should consider whether they require:
considerItems: Existing mountings that must be accommodated
Visual characteristics not completely represented by a report

certification.title: Certification and Documentation Requirements
certification.para1: Documentation requirements can vary depending on the diamond's size, value, intended market and customer expectations. Some buyers require individual grading reports for centre stones. Other applications may use commercial documentation suitable for smaller or calibrated diamonds.
certification.considerLabel: Before meeting Uniglo Diamonds, buyers should identify:
considerItems: Whether individual grading reports are required
Whether documentation must accompany each stone
Requirements for matched pairs or layouts
certification.para2: Documentation should be discussed at the beginning of the sourcing process rather than after a selection has already been prepared.

inPerson.title: Why Examine Diamonds in Person?
inPerson.para1: Online inventories make it easier to begin diamond research, but direct examination remains valuable for professional sourcing. In person, a buyer can evaluate a diamond's outline, proportions, brightness, pattern and overall visual character. Fancy-shaped diamonds particularly benefit from direct comparison because stones with similar measurements can differ in shape appeal and light distribution.
inPerson.understandLabel: Meeting a supplier also gives buyers an opportunity to understand:
understandItems: How available diamonds are selected and evaluated
Which grading laboratories accompany specific stones
Whether matched pairs or layouts can be supplied
Which sizes and qualities are currently available
How commercial and higher-value requirements differ
How future sourcing conversations will be handled
inPerson.outro: A productive sourcing meeting should provide clarity about both the stone and the supplier behind it.
inPerson.imageAlt: Hybrid natural-diamond sourcing at the Hong Kong show

antwerp.title: Antwerp Diamond Expertise in an International Sourcing Market
antwerp.para1: Hong Kong is one of the jewellery industry's most important international sourcing destinations, while Antwerp has played a central role in the global diamond trade for generations.
antwerp.para2: Uniglo Diamonds' Antwerp background connects the business with one of the world's most established diamond-trading centres. However, location alone does not create a successful supplier relationship.
antwerp.para3: Buyers also require clear communication, correctly understood specifications, realistic delivery expectations and dependable follow-up. Uniglo Diamonds approaches sourcing by first understanding the buyer's intended product, market and customer.
antwerp.para4: This allows the team to consider which shapes, measurements, quality combinations and supply arrangements may be most appropriate — supporting a retailer sourcing individual centre stones, a manufacturer preparing a repeat collection, a wholesaler serving several markets or a designer developing a specialised diamond-led range.

hybrid.title: A Hybrid Sourcing Experience Beyond the Exhibition Hall
hybrid.para1: The Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show operates through HKTDC's EXHIBITION+ format, extending the event beyond the physical exhibition.
hybrid.para2: The Click2Match business-matching platform is scheduled to operate from 23 February to 13 March 2027. The broader HKTDC sourcing extension is listed from 2 February to 1 April 2027.
hybrid.benefitsLabel: These online periods can help buyers:
benefits: Continue conversations after the physical exhibition
Connect with suppliers they could not meet onsite
hybrid.para3: The online platform supports the physical show rather than replacing it. Diamonds and gemstones often still benefit from direct examination before an important purchasing decision is made.
hybrid.imageAlt: Hybrid natural-diamond sourcing at the Hong Kong show

registration.title: Registration and Visitor Preparation
registration.para1: The Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show is a trade-focused sourcing event. Visitors should complete HKTDC buyer registration and review the current admission rules before travelling.
registration.para2: HKTDC has traditionally required badge validation using an original passport or Hong Kong Identity Card. Copies or alternative identity documents may not be accepted. Visitors should check the final 2027 rules before arriving at the venue.
prepareItems: Review the current admission and identity requirements
Check whether their badge covers both Twin Jewellery Shows
Review the 2027 exhibitor directory when published
Confirm Uniglo Diamonds' hall and stand number
Arrange important sourcing meetings in advance
Prepare preferred shapes, sizes, grades and quantities
Allow travel time between AsiaWorld-Expo and HKCEC
Review the final transport and shuttle information
Use Click2Match to prepare and follow up on meetings
registration.note: Buyers with specific natural-diamond requirements should share them with Uniglo Diamonds before the event where possible.

partnerships.title: Relationships Built Through Informed Sourcing
partnerships.para1: International exhibitions create opportunities to meet new suppliers, but strong sourcing relationships require more than an initial introduction. Consistency, transparency, communication and dependable service all become important once the exhibition ends.
partnerships.para2: For Uniglo Diamonds, returning to Hong Kong is an opportunity to reconnect with established partners and meet retailers, wholesalers and manufacturers discovering the company for the first time.
partnerships.nextStepsLabel: After meeting Uniglo Diamonds, buyers may wish to:
nextSteps: Request a more focused diamond selection
Schedule another viewing or sourcing conversation
partnerships.para3: These conversations help Uniglo Diamonds understand how demand differs between markets while continuing to support buyers with natural diamonds selected for real commercial requirements.

lookingAhead.title: Looking Ahead to Hong Kong 2027
lookingAhead.para1: From 2–6 March 2027, the Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show will bring the international sourcing community together at AsiaWorld-Expo.
lookingAhead.para2: Uniglo Diamonds looks forward to presenting a carefully selected natural-diamond portfolio and meeting buyers, manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers, designers and other jewellery professionals.
lookingAhead.para3: Whether you are searching for an individual documented diamond, matched stones, calibrated diamonds, commercial requirements or natural diamonds for a planned jewellery collection, we invite you to meet the Uniglo Diamonds team in Hong Kong.
lookingAhead.note: The confirmed Uniglo Diamonds stand number and appointment information will be published on this page once available.

items.question: When is the Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show 2027?
items.answer: The physical exhibition will take place from Tuesday, 2 March through Saturday, 6 March 2027.

items.question: Where will the show be held?
items.answer: The Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show 2027 will be held at AsiaWorld-Expo, located near Hong Kong International Airport.

items.question: What are the opening hours?
items.answer: The published schedule lists 10:30–18:30 on 2 March, 10:00–18:30 from 3–5 March, and 10:00–17:30 on 6 March. Visitors should verify the final hours before attending.

items.question: What can buyers source at the exhibition?
items.answer: The show focuses on loose diamonds, coloured gemstones, pearls, laboratory-grown diamonds, synthetic gemstones and jewellery-making materials.

items.question: Is this the same as the Hong Kong International Jewellery Show?
items.answer: No. The Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show takes place at AsiaWorld-Expo from 2–6 March and focuses primarily on loose materials. The Hong Kong International Jewellery Show takes place at HKCEC from 4–8 March and focuses primarily on finished jewellery.

items.question: What are the HKTDC Twin Jewellery Shows?
items.answer: The Twin Jewellery Shows are the Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show and the Hong Kong International Jewellery Show. Together, they cover loose materials and finished jewellery across two venues.

items.question: Do the two exhibitions overlap?
items.answer: Yes. Both shows operate from 4–6 March 2027. Buyers planning to attend both should account for travel time between AsiaWorld-Expo and HKCEC.

items.question: Is the exhibition open to the public?
items.answer: The Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show is positioned as a trade-focused sourcing event. Visitor eligibility and admission conditions should be verified through the official 2027 registration information before travelling.

items.question: What identification is required?
items.answer: HKTDC has traditionally required buyers to validate their badges in person using an original passport or Hong Kong Identity Card. Visitors should confirm the final 2027 documentation rules before attending.

items.question: When is Click2Match available?
items.answer: The published 2027 schedule lists Click2Match from 23 February to 13 March 2027.

items.question: What is Uniglo Diamonds' stand number?
items.answer: Uniglo Diamonds' 2027 hall and stand number have not yet been publicly confirmed. This page will be updated when the information becomes available.

items.question: What natural diamonds can buyers discuss with Uniglo Diamonds?
items.answer: Buyers can discuss Round Brilliant and fancy-shaped natural diamonds across different sizes, measurements, colours and clarities. Requirements may include individual documented stones, matched pairs, calibrated diamonds and multi-stone selections.

items.question: Can buyers discuss matched or calibrated diamonds?
items.answer: Yes. Buyers can discuss matched pairs, coordinated side stones, calibrated selections and layouts for multi-stone jewellery.

items.question: Can manufacturers discuss repeat-supply requirements?
items.answer: Yes. Manufacturers should provide their required shapes, measurements, quality ranges, quantities and production schedules when discussing repeat supply.

items.question: Should buyers arrange a meeting with Uniglo Diamonds?
items.answer: An appointment is recommended for buyers with specific shape, quality, measurement, quantity or price requirements. Meeting information will be added after Uniglo Diamonds' 2027 stand details are confirmed.

finalCta.title: Meet Uniglo Diamonds in Hong Kong
finalCta.para: Meet Uniglo Diamonds at the Hong Kong International Diamond, Gem & Pearl Show 2027 to explore natural diamonds and Antwerp-based sourcing possibilities. Prepare your preferred shapes, measurements, quality ranges, documentation requirements and intended jewellery applications so the team can plan a more relevant discussion.
